name: run_002
why: The full 180 second shot table of knowledge/DEMO-SCRIPT.md section 3, played in one take on the build: the title, the crawl, the drive, the walk to the quay checkpoint, the gate and its three replies, the dock office and the boarding pass, the TALK fight won by talking, the deck hound won by one FIGHT, the ship's log save, and the defeat that opens the game over. Card t_785b61f0. It is not run_001: that one is 71 s and is pinned as the walk take, and this one is the submission take.
beat_source: knowledge/mechanics/PACING-AND-CUTSCENES.md section 9 (the 32 beat sheet) and knowledge/DEMO-SCRIPT.md section 3 (S1 to S6, second by second)

game.env_note: No PP_ROUTE_HOLD and no PP_SLICE: this run follows data/slice.json as a player does. The crawl hands to the drive, the drive to the arrival, the arrival's map trigger to the gate, the gate to the office, the office to the boarding, and the boarding to the deck, where the map's own touch triggers start the three fights.

clock.note: 180 s is 10,800 steps at 60 a second, the game's own step rate (spec 05, spec 07)

seeds.note: title_flash is PP_TITLE_FLASH_SEED, so the attract's lightning flashes on the same steps. The encounter stream is the encounter row's own seed (data/encounters/all.json: tutorial_sailors 20261019, deck_hound 20261022, percy 771), which the build pins by data and not by this file.

talk.note: The TALK fight's replies are baked rows in this build (data/meta_bake.json, the replay leg of spec 19) unless tools/ai_bridge.py is up on 127.0.0.1:8791 with a model key in the environment. The run records whichever leg it actually took and says which in the verify file.

record.note: 768x720 is 3x the 256x240 screen. min_seconds 170 is the bottom of the card's 170 to 190 band and the end step is 10,800, which is 180.0 s: the middle of the band.

checks.note: palette_share_min is 0.55 and not run_001's 0.90: the quay and the battle field are drawn with roles the room palette set does not carry, and the measured fight frames sit at 0.39 to 0.40. The checks that catch a wrong take are the beats, the footsteps and the run's own failures.

cancel held: the drive is skipped the way a player skips it
the drive's own line that the player skipped it
the quay loads at the spawn tile 24,1 and the gate trigger is at 8,10, so the walk is nine tile rows down and then sixteen tiles west along row 10, where the checkpoint tile sits
down held 69 steps: nine tile rows, landing the feet in row 10 at py 154 (75 steps lands him in row 11 and the gate is never touched, which is what the 07:46 take did)

left held 128 steps: sixteen tiles west along row 10 from the spawn column 24 (px 384), stopping ON the checkpoint tile 8,10 (px 128, py 154), because quay_gate_checkpoint is a scene trigger and a scene trigger fires on confirm, never on the walk over it: 24 steps stopped on 21,10 after the map moved the start spawn west to 24,1, and the confirm there found no trigger underfoot and the route stalled on the field. The leg is 104 steps longer than the 2026-10-27 take, so the firing confirm lands at 44.73 s and not at 43.00 s, still inside S4's beat window (knowledge/DEMO-SCRIPT.md line 125, 0:39.03 to 1:19.03)

the feet are on the checkpoint tile and the hero faces west along row 10, so the reach box covers 7,10 (no trigger) and the tile underfoot (quay_gate_checkpoint). No marker is named here: a map step never hands on (pp_route_take_next is called only by a scene or a fight ending), so 'step arrival handed to step gate' was a line this build can never print, and naming it made every later marker report a failure

Confirm standing on the checkpoint: this is the press that fires quay_gate_checkpoint, so the gate scene and its box start here and the six page presses below turn what it opened (13 confirms at this beat, one more than the 12 the 07:46 take sent, which left the bluff reply's last page unturned and the scene never ended)
